cues.en: Would you do me a favor? I'd like to stop talking for a minute, and when I do, take a look at the room you're in, and above all, at the man-made objects in that room that surround you. The television set, the lights, the phone, and so on. And ask yourself what those objects do to your life just because they're there. Go ahead. Well, that is what this series is going to be all about. It's about the things that surround you in the modern world, and just because they're there,
cues.zh: 能帮我个忙吗？我想先停一分钟不说话，趁这个时候，请你看看你所在的房间，尤其看看房间里围绕着你的人造物品。电视机、灯、手机等等。然后问问自己，这些物品仅仅因为摆在那里，对你的生活做了什么。来吧。而这正是本系列要讲的全部内容。它讲的是现代世界中围绕在你身边的东西，仅仅因为它们在那里，

cues.en: shape the way you think and behave and why they exist in the form they do and who or what was responsible for them existing at all. The search for those clues will take us all over the world and 12,000 years into the past because it's in those strange places and in those long gone centuries that the secret of the modern world lies. And you never believe the extraordinary things that led to us being the way we are today. Things like, for instance,
cues.zh: 就塑造了你的思维和行为方式，以及它们为何以这样的形态存在，又是谁或什么促成了它们的存在。寻找这些线索将带我们走遍世界，深入一万两千年前的过去，因为现代世界的秘密就藏在那些奇异之地和那些逝去的世纪里。你绝不会相信那些让我们成为今天这样的非凡事物。比如说，

cues.en: Why a 16th century doctor at the court of Queen Elizabeth did something that made it possible for you to watch this screen now? Or the fact that because 18th century merchants were worried about ships' bottoms, you have nylon to wear? Or why a group of French monks and their involvement with sheep rearing helped to give the modern world the computer? Or what medieval Europeans did with their fire in winter that led to motor car manufacture?
cues.zh: 为什么伊丽莎白女王宫廷里的一位16世纪医生做了一件事，让你现在能看着这个屏幕？或者，因为18世纪的商人担心船底，你才有了尼龙衣服穿？又或者，为什么一群法国修士和他们养羊的经历帮助现代世界得到了计算机？再或者，中世纪欧洲人冬天用火的方式如何促成了汽车制造？

cues.en: The story of the events and the people who over centuries came together to bring us in from the cold and to wrap us in a warm blanket of technology is a matter of vital importance. Since more and more of that technology infiltrates every aspect of our lives, it's become a life support system without which we can't survive. And yet, how much of it do we understand? Do I bother myself with the reality of what happens when I get into a big steel box, press a button and rise into the sky?
cues.zh: 几个世纪以来，事件和人物共同书写的故事，将我们从寒冷中带入，用技术的温暖毯子将我们包裹，这至关重要。随着这项技术日益渗透到我们生活的方方面面，它已成为我们不可或缺的生命支持系统。然而，我们对其了解多少呢？当我坐进一个巨大的钢铁盒子，按下按钮，升入天空时，我是否会去思考背后发生的现实呢？

cues.en: Of course I don't. I take going up in the world like that for granted. We all do. And as the years of the 20th century have gone by, the things we take for granted have multiplied way beyond the ability of any individual to understand in a lifetime. The things around us, the man-made inventions we provide ourselves with, are like a vast network, each part of which is interdependent with all the others. I mean, cross the road. Whether or not a car coming round the corner knocks you down.
cues.zh: 当然不会。我理所当然地认为这样升入世界是自然而然的事。我们都是如此。随着20世纪岁月的流逝，我们认为理所当然的事物已经成倍增长，远远超出了任何人在一生中能够理解的范围。我们周围的事物，我们为自己提供的人造发明，就像一个庞大的网络，其中每个部分都与其他所有部分相互依存。我的意思是，过马路时，是否会被拐角处驶来的车撞倒，

cues.en: may have something to do with the person you've never met fitting the brakes correctly. Change anything in that network and the effects spread like ripples on a pond. And all the things in that network have become so specialised that only the people involved in making them understand them. I don't mean use them, anybody can use them. Down there is one of the biggest, most complex cities in the world full of people using things as if they understood them and sometimes not even knowing they're doing it.
cues.zh: 可能与你从未谋面的人是否正确安装刹车有关。改变这个网络中的任何东西，其影响都会像池塘中的涟漪一样扩散开来。而且，这个网络中的所有事物都变得如此专业化，只有参与制造它们的人才能真正理解它们。我指的不是使用它们，任何人都能使用。下面就是世界上最大、最复杂的城市之一，到处都是使用各种事物的人，他们好像理解这些事物，有时甚至不知道自己在做什么。

cues.en: New York City, like all the other major high-density population centers scattered across the earth, is a technology island. It can either feed nor clothe nor house nor warm its inhabitants without supplies from outside. Without those supplies, the entire massive structure and the teeming millions it encloses would die. And yet, in cities everywhere, we act as if that were not so. We have no choice. The pace of life in New York is set by the pace of the technology that serves it.
cues.zh: 纽约市，就像地球上其他所有散布的高密度人口中心一样，是一座技术孤岛。没有外界的供应，它就无法提供食物、衣物、住所或取暖。没有这些供应，整个庞大的结构及其包围的数百万居民都将灭亡。然而，在各地的城市中，我们表现得好像并非如此。我们别无选择。纽约的生活节奏是由服务于它的技术节奏决定的。

cues.en: You just have to hope it'll stay that way. I'd like you to meet a few people who were in or near New York City on a November evening over a decade ago. And the reason I'd like you to meet them is because they all have one thing in common. They were all brought to a sudden and catastrophic realization of how vulnerable they were. How dependent on one aspect of that technological network I was talking about. Because of what this did to their lives. Now until I was told what this is,
cues.zh: 你只能希望它能一直这样。我想让你们见几个人，十多年前一个十一月的晚上，他们在纽约市或附近。我想让你们见他们的原因是，他们都有一个共同点。他们都突然而灾难性地意识到自己有多么脆弱。多么依赖我所说的那个技术网络的一个方面。因为这对他们的生活造成了什么影响。现在，直到有人告诉我这是什么，

cues.en: I was no more able to recognize what it is than you are now. But watch what it did to those people. And if you look very carefully, you'll see evidence of what this does in every second of what follows now. It's one minute past five in the evening, rush hour in downtown Manhattan. 800,000 people crowd onto subways, looking forward to home, to the end of this journey. For most of them, the technology carrying them doesn't exist. They take it for granted. Two minutes.
cues.zh: 我才像你们现在一样无法认出它是什么。但看看它对那些人做了什么。如果你仔细观察，你会看到这在接下来的每一秒中都有证据。现在是下午五点过一分，曼哈顿市中心的交通高峰期。80万人挤上地铁，期待着回家，期待这段旅程的结束。对他们大多数人来说，载着他们的技术并不存在。他们视之为理所当然。两分钟。

cues.en: past five. Kennedy Airport, the usual evening departure rate. Passengers with appointments in New Delhi, London, Tokyo. Appointments they expect to keep. And 200 planes due to arrive in the next five hours. No delays expected. Three minutes past five. At the Energy Control Centre downtown, nothing special is happening. It's the standard rush hour condition in the main control room. The time of day when power consumption started to come up to a maximum.
cues.zh: 五点已过。肯尼迪机场，傍晚时分的常规离港节奏。乘客们要去新德里、伦敦、东京赴约。他们期待能守时的约会。未来五小时内，有200架飞机预计抵达。预计无延误。五点零三分。市中心的能源控制中心，一切如常。主控制室里是标准的晚高峰状态。一天中电力消耗开始攀升至峰值的时刻。

cues.en: as people head for home and meals get cooked. It's cool outside. After a high of 58, the temperature's falling to an expected low of 39, with a predicted wind chill factor of 5 degrees. The energy levels are more than enough to cook, even on a chilly November evening. Ten past five, Mount Sinai Hospital. The patient, Mrs. Markana, is expecting twins. Thank you, Mr. Chairman.
cues.zh: 人们赶回家做饭。外面很凉爽。在达到58度的高点后，气温预计降至39度的低点，预测的风寒指数为5度。即便是11月的寒冷夜晚，能源水平也足以应对烹饪所需。五点十分，西奈山医院。病人马卡纳夫人正期待着一对双胞胎的到来。谢谢您，主席先生。

cues.en: May I first say to my distinguished colleague the ambassador from the USSR? 12 minutes past 5, the UN General Assembly in session. The speaker is President Roosevelt's son. In their boxes, the interpreters, the invisible support structure of the debate, whatever the language, at the UN, that's taken for granted.
cues.zh: 首先，我要向尊敬的同僚——苏联大使致辞吗？五点十二分，联合国大会正在进行。发言者是罗斯福总统的儿子。同传箱里，口译员们是辩论背后无形的支撑结构，无论何种语言，在联合国，这一切都被视为理所当然。

cues.en: In the subway, Herbert Friedman, a lawyer, reads his paper on his way home to suburban Jamaica. Al Haneck works for a publisher on Fifth Avenue. He passes the time doing a crossword. Marjorie O'Shaughnessy also works for a publisher, looking forward to spending a quiet evening at home. Steve Boetti, late, into a movie. Bruce Singer works in Greenwich Village. Bill Palmer is a student, just been playing basketball. And Hans Kramer, insurance broker. All these people take the subway every evening.
cues.zh: 地铁上，律师赫伯特·弗里德曼在回家的路上读着报纸，目的地是郊区的牙买加。阿尔·哈内克在第五大道的一家出版社工作。他以填字游戏消磨时光。玛乔丽·奥肖内西同样在出版社工作，期待着在家度过一个宁静的夜晚。史蒂夫·博埃蒂迟到了，正赶往电影院。布鲁斯·辛格在格林威治村工作。比尔·帕尔默是一名学生，刚打完篮球。还有汉斯·克莱默，保险经纪人。这些人每晚都乘坐地铁。

cues.en: They expect to get home. They always do. 5.15 at Kennedy Airport. At one of the international terminals, on the board, Scandinavian Airlines 9-11. Scandinavian 9-11 is on its way into Kennedy. The pilot is veteran Captain Karl Lofstedt.
cues.zh: 他们都盼着回家。一向如此。5点15分，肯尼迪机场。在一个国际航站楼的显示屏上，北欧航空9-11航班。北欧航空9-11正在飞抵肯尼迪机场。飞行员是资深机长卡尔·洛夫斯泰特。

cues.en: A clear moonlit night. The flight manifest lists 89 passengers. The descent into Kennedy is so far uneventful. It's now 15 minutes and 30 seconds past five.
cues.zh: 晴朗的月夜。航班名单上有89名乘客。飞抵肯尼迪的下降过程迄今平安无事。现在是5点15分30秒。

cues.en: With the next contraction there, you'll take a deep breath and push real hard, okay? I think one is about to start. Take a deep breath and push real hard. At Mount Sinai Hospital, Mrs. Marcano is in labor.
cues.zh: 下一次宫缩来的时候，你要深吸一口气，使劲推，好吗？我看马上就要开始了。深吸一口气，使劲推。在西奈山医院，马卡诺夫人正在分娩。

cues.en: The anesthetic being used at the time is a mixture of gases including one called cyclopropane. It's potentially explosive, but everybody knows that.
cues.zh: 当时使用的麻醉剂是混合气体，其中包括一种叫环丙烷的气体。它有爆炸的危险，但这一点人人都知道。

cues.en: It's now exactly 16 minutes and 10 seconds past five. One second later, several hundred miles northwest of New York City, this did what it was built to do with disastrous consequences. You may have already guessed what kind of technological network this is part of. It's a bit of a power station. The power station known as Adam Beck 2 here at Niagara
cues.zh: 现在正好是5点16分10秒。一秒钟后，在纽约市西北数百英里处，这个装置做了它本该做的事，造成了灾难性的后果。你可能已经猜到了这是哪一种技术网络的一部分。它有点像一座发电站。这座发电站叫亚当·贝克2号，位于尼亚加拉

cues.en: where electricity is generated by the tremendous power of falling water. The water turns turbine blades that make a shaft spin at the top of the shaft are magnets and they spin inside a cylinder up there that has copper wire coils on its inner wall. The interaction between the spinning magnets and the copper coils makes electricity. That's where this comes in. It's a relay and its job is to detect changes in power
cues.zh: 这里的电力由落水的巨大力量产生。水流带动涡轮叶片，使一根轴旋转，轴顶上是磁铁，它们在上方一个内壁装有铜线圈的圆筒内旋转。旋转的磁铁与铜线圈之间的相互作用产生了电。这就是这个东西的用武之地。它是一个继电器，其职责是检测电力变化

cues.en: going onto a transmission line, these up here. Power flows north along these lines and on the particular evening in question this relay detected an increase in power on one of those lines that was above a preset limit. When that happened magnets set around this metal cup caused it to rotate and that brought this arm to make a contact like this. That contact was made on the evening of November the 9th 1965 at 16 minutes and 11 seconds past 5.
cues.zh: 也就是送入输电线路的电力变化，就是上面这些线路。电力沿着这些线路向北流动，而在那个特定的傍晚，这个继电器检测到其中一条线路上的电力增加，超过了预设限值。这时，围绕这个金属杯设置的磁铁使它旋转，从而使这个臂像这样接通。那次接通发生在1965年11月9日晚上5点16分11秒。

cues.en: The effect was to cascade power off the overloaded line and onto another, which overloaded and tripped the next, until all five lines going north had tripped out, dumping their entire load onto lines going south. Within seven seconds, the tremendous overload began to take out generating stations all over northeastern America, from Boston to New York, as the network fell apart. As each area went, it overloaded the next.
cues.zh: 结果就是，电力从过载的线路级联转移到另一条线路上，使其过载并跳闸，接着下一条也跳闸，直到向北的五条线路全部跳闸，把所有负荷都倾泻到向南的线路上。七秒之内，巨大的过载开始摧毁美国东北部从波士顿到纽约的各个发电站，整个网络土崩瓦解。每每一个区域崩溃，就会使下一个区域过载。

cues.en: Within 10 seconds, the only major system left was the great energy island of New York. As the network fell apart, links between one energy centre and another broke. Instead of 300,000 kilowatts coming into New York to help meet demand, one and a half million kilowatts were draining out of the city to supply areas now cut off from the network but still connected like leeches to the New York generators. As the overload hit the New York generators, they too began to trip out.
cues.zh: 十秒之内，仅存的主要系统就是纽约这个巨大的能源孤岛。随着网络崩溃，各能源中心之间的连接断开。原本有30万千瓦电力输入纽约以满足需求，现在却有150万千瓦从城市流出，供应那些已被切断网络、却仍像水蛭一样附着在纽约发电机上的地区。当过载波及纽约的发电机时，它们也开始跳闸。

cues.en: As the lifeblood of the city drained, it went into spasm. At the UN, chaos, the power to keep the lights on, also served the interpreters. Who in the growing darkness has, however I hope, brought a glimmer of light.
cues.zh: 随着城市的生命之血流失，它陷入了痉挛。在联合国，一片混乱，维持照明的电力也供给了口译员。在越来越深的黑暗中，是谁，我希望，带来了一丝光亮。

cues.en: And without interpreters, trapped in their darkened boxes, deprived of access to the ears of the delegates, the United Nations was suddenly and totally disunited, as completely as if at war. The city's elevators stopped. Perhaps the subways were the only technology that people expected to fail.
cues.zh: 没有了口译员——他们被困在黑暗的箱子里，无法传译给代表们听——联合国突然之间彻底分裂，如同处于战争状态一般。城市的电梯停了。也许地铁是人们唯一预料到会出故障的技术。

cues.en: 800,000 people were now deep in the ground under New York, caught in a technology trap most of them had never thought twice about. As light went, so did the one in Mrs. Markana's operating theater. It was now only 10 minutes since the crisis had been triggered by the relay at Niagara more than 500 miles away. The generators continued to trip out and at Kennedy Airport, the radar screens went black.
cues.zh: 80万人此刻正身处纽约地下的深处，陷入一个他们大多数人从未认真想过的技术陷阱。灯光熄灭的同时，马卡纳太太手术室里的灯也灭了。此时距离500多英里外尼亚加拉的那个继电器触发危机，仅仅过去了10分钟。发电机持续跳闸，肯尼迪机场的雷达屏幕也一片漆黑。

cues.en: and flight 911 was in trouble. Roll up, I got flag warning, switch number two through the ILA. Who we got? Yeah, John? Can you hold it at 250? I'll take 200 if I can. What time did it go out? A story of two and three went out. They can't hold on. By 528, the time had come to protect the system by deliberately switching what was left.
cues.zh: 911航班也陷入了麻烦。快过来，我收到了故障警告，把2号开关打到ILA。我们联系上谁了？是你吗，约翰？你能保持在250吗？可以的话我就降到200。什么时候断的？2号和3号都断了。他们撑不住了。到5点28分，是时候通过故意切断剩余部分来保护系统了。

cues.en: Over an area of 18 million square miles, 30 million people were now in darkness.
cues.zh: 在1800万平方英里的区域内，3000万人此刻陷入黑暗。

cues.en: Isolated from each other in small groups, millions of people were still unaware of the extent of the blackout, in the subway especially. People started chatting, but for the most part no one really got into it yet because we thought it was just another typical rush hour delay. But it was dark and that was kind of unsettling to be in such a crowd but not to be able to see anybody. So one of the women
cues.zh: 人们三五成群地彼此隔绝，数百万人仍不知道这场停电的范围有多大，尤其是在地铁里。人们开始聊起天来，但大多数人其实还没真正聊开，因为大家以为这不过是又一次典型的晚高峰延误。但周围一片漆黑，身处这么密集的人群中却谁也看不见，这让人有些不安。于是其中一位女士

cues.en: had candles in her bag. You know, I have some candles. Maybe we can light them. This abnormal business of actually talking to anybody on the subway caught on briefly all over New York. Let's put some light on the situation. My birthday anyway, anybody feel like singing happy birthday? Make a happy situation out of a terrible one. My name? Louise? Happy birthday to you. Happy birthday to you.
cues.zh: 包里有蜡烛。你知道，我有几根蜡烛。也许我们可以点上。这种在地铁上真跟人搭话的反常举动，在纽约各地短暂地流行开来。咱们给这局面添点光吧。反正今天是我生日，有谁想唱生日歌吗？把糟糕的局面变成欢乐的局面。我叫什么？路易丝？祝你生日快乐。祝你生日快乐。

cues.en: But while this journey had taken on a meaning nobody expected, so too at the hospital had Mrs. Markana's delivery of twins thanks to the anaesthetic. It was then a general scurry around to find flashlights and I immediately commandeered one so I could see what was happening. One of the nurses, if I shall never forget, walked into the room carrying a lighted candle. Put the candle out! Get out of here! What's going on? Get out of here! Just get out of my mind.
cues.zh: 但这段旅程有了谁都没想到的意义，医院里马卡纳太太也因麻醉剂顺利生下了双胞胎。当时大家四处慌忙找手电筒，我立刻抓了一支，好看清发生了什么。有位护士我永远忘不了，她端着一支点燃的蜡烛走进房间。把蜡烛灭掉！出去！怎么回事？出去！别再来烦我。

cues.en: I was blessed and so engaged and I had visions of all of us. The whole place blowing up in one great conflagration. The phone system was the only thing working, if you could get a number.
cues.zh: 我很幸运，也很投入，脑海中浮现出我们所有人的画面。整个地方在一场大火中爆炸。电话系统是唯一还能用的东西，前提是你打得通号码。

cues.en: And Captain Lofton was learning the full extent of his predicament. ILS, the landing aid that guided him in, wasn't there anymore. The extraordinary thing in the subways was that a full hour into the crisis, nobody was trying to escape from the trout.
cues.zh: 洛夫顿机长正逐渐认清自己处境的严重程度。引导他降落的仪表着陆系统已经不存在了。地铁里最离奇的是，危机发生整整一小时后，竟没人试图从车厢里逃出去。

cues.en: Now all we need is a knife. I think I have something for you. We need now the cups. Got a wish. The wish is that we get home tonight. I just assumed that something went wrong with the particular train that I was riding on.
cues.zh: 现在只差一把刀。我想我有你要的东西。现在需要杯子。许个愿吧。愿望是今晚能到家。我原本只以为是我坐的那趟列车出了点问题。

cues.en: There was a feeling of it's being something we all just had to wait out together. There was nothing anybody could do about it. No one knew anything about anything. I can carry napkins around. I wipe my seats off so I don't get my clothes dirty. Put yourself through this position. Would you do any different? Here they were, one hour into a major disaster, and still trying to laugh their way out of it. Drink a wine in the subway outside of it. If anybody's driving, don't drink. How about singing a song?
cues.zh: 当时有种感觉，这事只能大家一起熬过去。谁都无能为力。没人知道任何情况。我可以随身带着餐巾。我擦擦座位，免得弄脏衣服。设身处地想想。你会做得不一样吗？事到如今，重大灾难发生一小时了，他们还在努力用笑声化解。在地铁外面喝点酒吧。要是有人开车，就别喝。要不唱首歌吧？

cues.en: People began to be very jovial and began to sing Show me the way to go home and everything that people could think of that related to our flight At the hospital darkness made no difference
cues.zh: 人们开始非常欢快，唱起《Show Me the Way to Go Home》，还有所有能想到的跟我们飞行有关的歌。在医院里，黑暗没什么影响。

cues.en: Well, the baby was delivered without the lights because you didn't need the lights for the delivery. That's manipulative. Remember, you're reaching up into the uterus, grabbing a foot which is strictly by feel. You rupture the membranes and you bring the foot down. The second baby was vigorous and then we repaired the piece.
cues.zh: 嗯，孩子是在没灯的情况下接生的，因为接生并不需要灯。这全靠手法。记住，你要伸手进子宫，完全凭触感抓住一只脚。你破膜，把脚拉下来。第二个孩子很有活力，然后我们修补了那个部位。

cues.en: Captain Lofsted had only a few seconds left to make his decision. He was at 2,000 feet, past the airport and heading straight for Manhattan in the darkness. There was only one thing he could do. Lofsted and 200 other jets that night landed with the help of radio working on planes sitting on the ground. In the subway, people were still coping. About after an hour, an hour and a half, people became very restless.
cues.zh: Lofsted 机长只剩几秒钟做决定。他当时在2000英尺高度，已经飞过机场，在黑暗中直奔曼哈顿。他只能做一件事。那晚，Lofsted 和另外200架喷气机借助停在地面的飞机上的无线电降落。在地铁里，人们还在勉强应对。大约一到一个半小时后，人们变得非常焦躁。

cues.en: It was not pleasant. It was not very congenial, but everybody felt scared. Never been this late to let you sit here and wonder and wonder and send nobody down to help us. Somebody knock on the window, see if you're going to turn to his attention. After about an hour and a half of this, train employees would pass outside, but not look at us and not answer us when people banged on the windows and called out.
cues.zh: 那感觉不好，也很不友好，但大家都害怕。从来没这么晚过，让你坐在这儿想了又想，却没人下来帮我们。有人敲窗户，看你是否会理会。这样过了大约一个半小时后，列车员会从外面经过，但当人们敲窗呼喊时，他们不看我们，也不回答。

cues.en: They just ignored us. I think he's the conductor from the train, but I'm not sure. Maybe he's gone for help. I don't know. Gradually, finally, people began to realize where they were. Lost, under the ground, helpless, unless help came. When we have a major power blackout, it at least hits the entire city. It's all relaxed. We'll be trying to get you off as soon as possible. We would have to be in between stations. How can we be on a platform? I don't know.
cues.zh: 他们完全没理我们。我想他是列车上的列车员，但我不确定。也许他去找人帮忙了。我不知道。渐渐地，人们终于开始意识到自己身在何处。迷失在地下，无助，除非有人来救。遇到大停电时，至少会波及整座城市。大家都放松点。我们会尽快把你们救出来。我们肯定是在两站之间。我们怎么可能在站台上呢？我不知道。

cues.en: This is how long this will take. It's carnatic and it affects the entire city. We have people coming by evacuating the trains now. Please relax. Mrs. Makana found out what had happened to her, though not the way she expected. Mrs. Makana, who was that? When I woke up and I saw all the candles lit around the room, I thought I was dead and there was a priest standing nearby.
cues.zh: 这要花这么长时间。这是灾难性的，影响整座城市。现在有人正在疏散列车。请放松。Makana太太得知了自己遭遇了什么，虽然不是她预料的方式。Makana太太，那是谁？我醒来时看到房间里点满了蜡烛，我以为自己死了，旁边站着一位神父。

cues.en: and for a minute there I thought he had come to give me my last rights and I was afraid that all my family knew that I was dead and they came to light candles for me. No, no, no, you don't have to pay more, you don't have to pay more. Don't be frightened now, you're going to be okay. And finally, as in all good fairy stories, it was over. Exactly about five hours after the train stopped about 10.30, the train began to empty by having all the passengers walk out singly upon the catwalk.
cues.zh: 有那么一会儿我以为他是来给我做临终圣事的，我害怕所有家人都知道我死了，他们来为我点蜡烛。不，不，不，你不用多付钱，你不用多付钱。现在别害怕，你会没事的。最后，就像所有美好的童话故事一样，一切结束了。大约在列车停下五小时后，也就是10点30分左右，列车开始清空，所有乘客一个接一个地走上通道。

cues.en: A few days later, people were back at their daily routine as if it had never happened. The night New York became a trap, forgotten. This is one of the more perfect examples of the kind of technological trap that we set for ourselves. The lift, the elevator. I mean, what is it? It's a steel box with some buttons in it and maybe a trap door for emergencies, but whoever looks that close. Except when this happens, where is it? And even in this situation,
cues.zh: 几天后，人们又回到了日常生活的轨道，仿佛一切从未发生过。纽约变成陷阱的那一夜，被遗忘了。这是我们从自身所设的技术陷阱中，所能找到的最完美的例子之一。电梯，升降机。我是说，它是什么？它就是个铁盒子，里面有些按钮，也许还有个供紧急情况用的活板门，但谁会看得那么仔细。除非发生这种事，它在哪儿？而即便在这种情况下，

cues.en: closed in with an escape route that we can't handle. We behave like many of those New Yorkers did. We strike a light and we look around to see how badly things are. And if we find, in this case, an emergency button, absolutely great. We sit back and we wait for help to come. We wait for technology to come back and save our lives because it's inconceivable that it won't, isn't it? I mean, if you admit that, you've got to admit
cues.zh: 被困其中，明明有逃生通道，我们却不知所措。我们的反应就像许多纽约人一样。我们点亮灯火，环顾四周，看看情况有多糟。如果在这种情况下，我们找到了紧急按钮，那真是太好了。我们靠回去，等待救援到来。我们等待技术回来拯救我们的生命，因为无法想象它不会来，不是吗？我是说，如果你承认这一点，你就得承认

cues.en: that every single day of your life, in some form or other, you unconsciously walk yourself into a technology trap because that's the only way to live in the modern world. So you don't admit it. You say, oh, well, in this situation, we'll cope. But what happens when the effects become widespread, irreversible, devastating? What happens when what little resources you have to help you cope give up? Then what?
cues.zh: 在你生命中的每一天，以某种形式，你都在无意识地走进一个技术陷阱，因为那是生活在现代世界的唯一方式。所以你不承认。你说，哦，好吧，在这种情况下，我们能应付。但当影响变得广泛、不可逆转、毁灭性时，会发生什么？当你用来帮助自己应付的仅有的一点资源也耗尽时，会发生什么？然后呢？

cues.en: Well in all the disaster scenarios you read what happens is that without power Technologically based civilization cracks up rapidly without enough auxiliary power and most major cities don't have it Organization is impossible. It's every man for himself looting and arson follow and in a city not prepared to be a fortress supplies run out fast and However frightening the thought of leaving your technological womb sooner or later. There is nowhere to go but out
cues.zh: 在你读过的所有灾难场景中，发生的情况是：没有电力，以技术为基础的文明会迅速崩溃；而没有足够的备用电源——大多数主要城市都没有——组织是不可能的。人人自顾不暇，抢劫和纵火随之而来；在一个没有准备成为堡垒的城市里，物资很快就会耗尽。然而，离开你的技术子宫这个想法无论多么可怕，迟早，除了出去，无处可去

cues.en: away from the danger the minute you decide to move you're on your own in a way that no modern 20th century city dweller has ever been in his life and then the traps begin to close to start with do you even know where to go in order to survive did you manage to get a map before you left and if you did how do you get out walk drive until you run out of fuel are you ahead of the millions of other people pouring down these roads trying to do just what you're trying to do
cues.zh: 远离危险。你决定行动的那一刻，你就只能靠自己了，这是任何现代20世纪城市居民一生中从未经历过的。然后陷阱开始闭合。首先，你甚至知道该去哪里才能生存吗？你离开前设法弄到地图了吗？如果弄到了，你怎么出去？步行？开车？直到燃料耗尽？你比涌上这些道路、试图做和你一样事情的数百万人领先吗？

cues.en: And if they catch up with you, have you got something they need? And if you have, can you protect yourself? Did you bring enough food and drink to last as long as necessary? And if you didn't, where will you get it? Steel? How far out will you have to push on until you're far enough out to be safe? And can you be sure that's far enough? And even if by some miracle you finally make it?
cues.zh: 如果他们追上你，你身上有他们需要的东西吗？如果有，你能保护自己吗？你带够了能撑到必要时候的食物和水吗？如果没带，你从哪里弄？钢铁？你得向外推进多远，才能远到安全？你能确定那够远吗？即便你奇迹般地终于成功了呢？

cues.en: Do you know enough to recognize a place to stop when you see it? I mean, what does Survival without technology look like? The veto signs up So let's say that finally somewhere far out into the country you come across a place that looks right And let's say that you've had the good sense and the good luck to to look for a farm Because that's where food comes from doesn't it? Okay, so it's a farm so you decide to stop Has anybody got there first are the owners still here because you're going to need shelter
cues.zh: 你真的知道该在什么时候停下吗？我的意思是，没有技术的生活是什么样子？否决牌上写着……假设你终于来到乡下很远的地方，遇到一个看起来不错的地方。假设你够明智也够幸运，去找一个农场，因为食物就是从那里来的，对吧？好，那是个农场，所以你决定停下来。有人先到那里了吗？主人还在吗？因为你需要住所。

cues.en: and people don't give their homes away, they barricade themselves in. So, sooner or later, exhausted and desperate, you may have to make the decision to give up and die, or to make somebody else give up and die because they won't accept you in their home voluntarily. And what in your comfortable urban life has ever prepared you for that decision? Okay, let's say by some miracle the place is empty and it's all yours. Is there enough food in the house? How long will it last? How will you cook it?
cues.zh: 而人们不会把自己的家让给别人，他们会把自己堵在里面。所以，迟早，在筋疲力尽和绝望中，你可能不得不决定放弃并死去，或者让别人放弃并死去，因为他们不会自愿接纳你进他们的家。你那舒适的城市生活里，有什么让你为这个决定做好了准备？好吧，假设奇迹般地，这个地方空无一人，全是你的了。房子里有足够的食物吗？能撑多久？你怎么做饭？

cues.en: Wood fires. Are you fit enough to chop all the wood you need before winter comes? If you're lucky, you've got livestock on the farm. Great. Meat. But can you slaughter and bleed and butcher an animal? Okay, supposing you manage that, you've got enough meat to eat until you've eaten all the cows. But at least you can start running your farm. But it's a modern farm, remember? It's mechanised. There's a gasoline pump, but it's empty. So you can't use the tractor. What you need is a horse and cart.
cues.zh: 木柴生火。你有足够的体力在冬天到来前劈好所有需要的木柴吗？如果幸运的话，农场里有牲畜。太好了。肉。但你能屠宰、放血和解剖一只动物吗？好，假设你做到了，你有足够的肉吃，直到你把所有的牛都吃完。但至少你可以开始经营你的农场了。但记住，这是现代农场。它是机械化的。有个汽油泵，但它是空的。所以你不能用拖拉机。你需要的是马和马车。

cues.en: But when did you last see a horse and cart on a modern farm? And everything else here. The saw, the power drills, the light, the steriliser, the water supply, the sewage system, the hoist, the milking parlour, the pumps, and everything on this control panel demands the one thing you don't have. Electric power. Everything on this farm that you found doesn't work. The place is a trap. But there's nowhere else to go.
cues.zh: 可是你上一次在现代农场里看到马和马车是什么时候？还有这里的一切。锯子、电钻、灯、消毒器、供水系统、排污系统、吊装设备、挤奶厅、水泵，还有这块控制面板上的一切，都需要一样你没有的东西。电力。你在这农场里找到的所有东西都运转不了。这地方是个陷阱。但你没别的地方可去。

cues.en: The only way you're going to survive is if you find the one thing you need to keep on providing the food you've got to have. And you don't need the mechanized version of that thing. You need the kind people haven't used in a hundred years. Ah, you need that kind of plow. You're saved. Or are you? Because what it comes down to at this point is this. Can you use a plow? It's taken a series of miracles just to get you this far, and here you are with the biggest miracle of all, a plow and animals to pull it.
cues.zh: 你唯一能活下来的办法，就是找到那件你需要的东西，好持续提供你必须拥有的食物。而你不需要那东西的机械化版本。你需要的是人们一百年都没用过的那种。啊，你需要那种犁。你得救了。真的吗？因为到这一步，归根结底就是这个问题。你会用犁吗？光是让你走到这一步，就已经是一连串奇迹了，而现在你面前摆着最大的奇迹，一把犁，还有拉犁的牲口。

cues.en: So maybe after a few days of fumbling around with the harnesses and the bits and pieces, you managed to yoke up the oxen and plough the land. And then and only then can you say that you have successfully escaped the wreckage of technological civilisation and lived off the land and survived. If you know how to use the furrow, you plough. I mean, can you tell the difference between an ear of corn and a geranium seed? Do you know when to sow whatever it is you think it is? Do you know when to harvest it and eat the bit that you think isn't poisonous? I mean, it's no accident.
cues.zh: 所以也许折腾了几天挽具和零零碎碎之后，你总算把牛套上了轭，把地犁了。只有到那时，你才能说自己成功逃离了技术文明的残骸，靠土地为生，活了下来。如果你懂得怎么用犁沟，你就犁地。我是说，你能分辨出一穗玉米和天竺葵种子吗？你知道什么时候该播种你以为的那东西吗？你知道什么时候该收割，该吃哪块你以为没毒的部分吗？我是说，这可不是偶然。

cues.en: that the chain of events triggered off by that relay in the power station back there in Niagara Falls ends here with the plow. The relay itself doesn't matter. I mean, any one of a million things could fail and cause our complex civilization to collapse for an hour, for a day, however long, because that's when you find out the extent to which you are reliant on technology and don't even know it. That's when you see that it's so interdependent, you take one thing away and the whole thing falls down and leaves you with nothing.
cues.zh: 由尼亚加拉瀑布那边发电站里的那个继电器所触发的一连串事件，最终在这里以这把犁收尾。继电器本身并不重要。我的意思是，上百万种东西里任何一个出故障，都可能让我们复杂的文明崩溃一小时、一天，或者不管多久，因为到那时你才会发现，自己有多依赖技术，甚至自己都没意识到。到那时你会看到，它是如此相互依赖：拿走一样东西，整个东西就垮掉，让你一无所有。

cues.en: unless you can plow and survive and start the whole process off again from scratch. And it's no accident that to do that you have to have a plow. Because it was the plow that triggered everything off, a long way back in the past, after a different set of people also found out that their comfortable life was falling apart. In a world where events came to a point where a fundamentally new way of life had to be found.
cues.zh: 除非你能犁地、活下来，并从头开始重启整个过程。而要做到这一点就必须有犁，这绝非偶然。因为正是犁触发了一切——那是在很久以前，在另一群人同样发现自己的舒适生活正在瓦解之后。当时，事情发展到了一个地步：必须找到一种全新的生活方式。

cues.en: That's exactly what happened about 12,000 years ago in maybe four places on the earth Northern India, Syria, Egypt, Central America It stopped raining and got very hot The result of that change in the weather was to lead to an invention that would trigger the development of a civilization that ends with that in the modern world Let me explain that
cues.zh: 大约12,000年前，地球上也许有四个地方发生了同样的事：印度北部、叙利亚、埃及、中美洲。雨停了，天气变得非常热。天气变化的结果，促成了一项发明；这项发明将触发文明的发展，而这个文明在现代世界最终以它收尾。让我解释一下。

cues.en: You see, the high grasslands started to dry out, became like this place, and the plants and the animals that had sustained the wandering tribes started to disappear. People began to die. There was only one thing the survivors could do, head for water. And so down they came into the great river valleys. Here in Egypt, that river was the Nile, and the Nile was an extraordinary river. It rose in two places. For one, it brought rotting vegetation, and for the other, potash.
cues.zh: 你看，高草原开始干涸，变得像这个地方一样，而支撑游牧部落的植物和动物开始消失。人们开始死亡。幸存者只能做一件事：去找水。于是他们一路下行，进入那些大河谷。在埃及这里，那条河就是尼罗河，而尼罗河是一条非凡的河。它从两个地方涨水：一处带来腐烂的植被，另一处带来钾盐。

cues.en: and any gardener will tell you what that means. When it flooded every year, it dumped compost and fertilizer onto the land. And the land bloomed. Too well. With easy food, the population grew to where not even the Nile could support it without help. Faced with starvation, the river dwellers tried planting grain by hand. Not enough. What solved their problem was an invention that triggered off a series of events which ends with us in our modern technology trap. Because that invention was to trigger...
cues.zh: 任何园丁都能告诉你这意味着什么。尼罗河每年泛滥时，会把堆肥和肥料冲到土地上。土地因此繁荣。太繁荣了。食物来得容易，人口增长到连尼罗河也无法独自养活的地步。面对饥荒，河边居民尝试手工种植谷物。不够。解决他们问题的是一项发明，它引发了一系列事件，最终让我们陷入现代技术陷阱。因为那项发明引发了……

cues.en: the beginnings of civilization. This is the first great man-made trigger of change, the plow. Because with it, you know how much harvest you're going to get next year. And because of that, you know you're going to be here next year. And because of that, you can plan for the future. And after a while, when you can produce surplus food, then that's when things really start to move in the tiny settlements. With regular food supplies, the population explodes.
cues.zh: 文明的起点。这是人类第一个伟大的人为变革触发器——犁。因为有了它，你知道明年能收获多少。正因为如此，你知道明年你还会在这里。也正因为如此，你可以为未来做规划。过了一段时间，当你能生产剩余食物时，小型定居点里的一切才真正开始动起来。有了稳定的食物供应，人口爆炸式增长。

cues.en: The village expands. There are more buildings and they're bigger for bigger families and they're more permanent. You domesticate animals for their milk and their meat and their skin because they're not there to hunt anymore. And basket weaving and the twisting of grass to do it teaches you how to spin flax and that makes linen. But it's the grain that causes the fundamental change because with it you bake the bread that is the staple diet on which everybody lives and you learn about ovens
cues.zh: 村庄扩张。建筑更多，也更大，容纳更大的家庭，而且更持久。你驯养动物，获取奶、肉和皮，因为已经不需要再去狩猎了。编篮子和拧草编的技艺教会你如何纺亚麻，从而织出亚麻布。但真正带来根本性变化的是谷物，因为有了它，你烤出面包——这是所有人赖以生存的主食——你也学会了使用烤炉，

cues.en: and about the effect of heat on mud and brick. But above all, you have to have somewhere to store the grain surplus in pots. But there's so much surplus by now, you need the pots to be made faster and you need them to last longer. So the potter's wheel happens. Then comes the problem of who does it belong to? And the only answer to that is this. Writing. And the very first writing takes that form. A name and a symbol for what's inside this pot or a lot of pots.
cues.zh: 以及热对泥和砖的影响。但最重要的是，你必须有个地方用陶罐储存剩余的谷物。可到这时剩余量已经太大，你需要陶罐做得更快，也需要它们更耐用。于是陶轮出现了。接着问题来了：这些东西归谁？唯一的答案就是这个。文字。而最早的文字正是这种形式。一个名字，加上一个符号，代表这个罐子或许多罐子里装的东西。

cues.en: or an entire village granary. And so the little villages grew with their huts and their granaries. And then, almost out of nowhere it seems, that happened. The oldest stone building in the world. The steppe pyramid of King Zozo at Sakara near Cairo. Built around 2700 BC. Instant sophisticated architecture from mud huts in one jump. How do they do it? Because of what they'd had to do to feed themselves, irrigate.
cues.zh: 或者一整个村庄的粮仓。于是小村庄们带着它们的小屋和粮仓发展起来。然后，几乎像是凭空出现一般，那件事发生了。世界上最古老的石头建筑。位于开罗附近萨卡拉的佐佐国王草原金字塔。建于公元前2700年左右。从泥屋一跃而成精致的建筑。他们是怎么做到的？因为他们为了养活自己、灌溉农田不得不做的事。

cues.en: Because the river flooded every year and destroyed landmarks and then retreated, leaving the soil to dry out, they had to do two things. Find a way of measuring the land so the farmer got his own fields back, and a way of channeling the water away for use after the flood had gone. The kind of measurement you need to do those things involves geometry and the type of mathematics a civil engineer uses. And building canals teaches you to work stone. If you know stonework and geometry and mathematics,
cues.zh: 因为河流每年泛滥，摧毁地标，然后退去，留下土壤变干，他们必须做两件事。找到一种测量土地的方法，好让农民收回自己的田地，以及一种在洪水退去后引水以供使用的方法。做这些事所需的测量涉及几何学以及土木工程师使用的那类数学。而修建运河教会你加工石头。如果你懂石工、几何和数学，

cues.en: You can build pyramids, especially if a strong central government that was developed to run the irrigation schemes in the first place tells you to. If the Pharaoh said he wanted a pointed stone monument, that's what he got. Funny thing is, the same drought that drove everybody down to the Nile also preserved the things they built, like their tombs, for thousands of years. The stuff on the walls in this tomb, for example, is 4,500 years old.
cues.zh: 你就能建造金字塔，尤其是当一个最初为管理灌溉工程而发展起来的强大中央政府命令你这么做的时候。如果法老说他要一座尖顶的石头纪念碑，他就会得到。有趣的是，正是那场驱使所有人迁到尼罗河边的干旱，也把他们建造的东西，比如他们的陵墓，保存了数千年。例如，这座陵墓墙上的东西已有4500年历史。

cues.en: a kind of cartoon view of the civilisation the plough created. I mean, look, here's the irrigation. There are these people carrying water pots, you see them? And they carry them across and they pour the water into a garden that has a wall round it. And then over here, look, there's a fellow doing a bit of weeding. There's the plough. They domesticated oxen. They tried to domesticate any animal that they could get their hands on. I mean, take a look at this. Animal flattened its back, tight back legs.
cues.zh: 这是一幅农耕文明催生的漫画式图景。看，这里是灌溉。有这些人扛着水罐，看到了吗？他们把水扛过去，倒进一个有围墙的园子里。再看这边，有个家伙在除草。这是犁。他们驯化了牛。凡是能抓到的动物，他们都想驯化。看看这个。动物被压平了背，后腿绷紧。

cues.en: hang on to its front legs, stuff food down its throat and hope it'll learn to love you. I didn't get too far with that one. It was a hyena. Well, you've got a growing community and plenty of spare food and you'll need to protect yourself. So making weapons becomes very important. And here on this wall, there's a whole thing about handling metals. Look, here are the weights and measures people checking on how much metal is going to be used. Next to them, the furnace men.
cues.zh: 抓住它的前腿，往它喉咙里塞食物，指望它能爱上你。这个我没搞成。那是只鬣狗。好了，你有了一个不断壮大的社群，还有充足的余粮，那你就得保护自己。所以制造武器变得非常重要。这面墙上，画的都是金属加工的事。看，这些是称重计量的人，在核算要用多少金属。旁边是炉工。

cues.en: You see the way they're raising the temperature? They're blowing on these tubes to create a draft in the furnace to get the temperature high. Next to them, here's the molten metal being poured into a mold. And here, the fella's beating it flat. Okay, you get yourself a kingdom, you get what you deserve, you get bureaucrats. Here they are, the scribes, writing everything down. See the pens behind their ears? In this case, they're noting taxes. Here are the people coming in to pay their taxes.
cues.zh: 看到他们怎么升温了吗？他们对着这些管子吹气，在炉子里形成气流，把温度升上去。旁边，熔化的金属正被倒进模具。这里，那家伙在把它敲平。好，你有了一个王国，你得到了你应得的——官僚。他们来了，是书吏，把一切都记下来。看到他们耳后的笔了吗？这里，他们在记录税收。这些是来交税的人。

cues.en: led persuasively by the local police. Here's a policeman with a rod of office. More policemen. Here's an Egyptian scruff of the neck. He obviously doesn't want to pay. If you end up not paying, they get out their whips and they tie you to a pole. And that's what you get for not coming up with the money. So you have a busy, sophisticated society. You have to have people at the top in charge. This is the tomb of one of them. He was a kind of Egyptian chancellor responsible directly to the king.
cues.zh: 由当地警察有说服力地带领。这里有一位手持权杖的警察。更多警察。这里有一个被抓住后颈的埃及人。他显然不想付钱。如果你最终不付钱，他们就会拿出鞭子，把你绑在柱子上。这就是你不掏钱的后果。所以你有一个繁忙、复杂的社会。你必须让上层的人来掌管。这是其中一人的陵墓。他是一种直接对国王负责的埃及宰相。

cues.en: There he is. His name was Meriruka. By sometime around 3200 BC, the entire 700 mile length of the Nile from the Mediterranean to Aswan was united and administered by officials like Meriruka, each one running what was called a water province, the section of the irrigation network and of the river under his command. What held it all together?
cues.zh: 他就在那里。他的名字叫梅里鲁卡。到公元前3200年左右，从地中海到阿斯旺的整条700英里长的尼罗河被像梅里鲁卡这样的官员统一管理，每个人管理一个所谓的“水省”，即他指挥下的灌溉网络和河流的一段。是什么把这一切维系在一起？

cues.en: was the king's magic ability as a god to come up year after year with an inundation of the Nile and to know exactly how high the waters would go. Of course, it wasn't magic, it was his astronomers. They observed that one particular star, Sirius, rises just before dawn on one particular day, the 17th of July, every year. And that day is one day before the flood begins. They also saw that, on average, the flood itself came once...
cues.zh: 是国王作为神明的魔力，能够年复一年地带来尼罗河的泛滥，并确切知道水位会涨多高。当然，这不是魔法，而是他的天文学家。他们观察到，一颗特定的星星——天狼星，每年7月17日黎明前升起。而那一天是洪水开始的前一天。他们还发现，平均而言，洪水本身每……

cues.en: every 365 days. Now, you put those two facts together, the star before dawn and the flood, and you've got yourself a calendar. And with a calendar, you can organize people. You can give them a date to do something on. And as for the king's ability to predict how high the water would go, well, you record the level of the flood every year with a scratch on the wall. And after a while, your experience will tell you early on how high the water's going to be later. Now, in Egypt, where water is life, that kind of knowledge
cues.zh: 365天来一次。现在，把这两个事实结合起来——黎明前的星星和洪水——你就有了一个日历。有了日历，你就可以组织人们。你可以给他们一个做某事的日期。至于国王预测水位会涨多高的能力，好吧，你每年在墙上划一道来记录洪水水位。过了一段时间，你的经验会早早告诉你水位以后会涨多高。现在，在埃及，水就是生命，那种知识

cues.en: and the ability to control gives you the power to build empires. These are the great ancient temples of Karnak on the edge of the Nile about 450 miles south of Cairo. They were the center of Egyptian religion built in the imperial city of Thebes when the Egyptian Empire was at its height, the greatest power in the world. This was the New York of the time. The temples were built over a period of about 2,000 years.
cues.zh: 和控制能力赋予你建立帝国的力量。这些是卡纳克伟大的古代神庙，位于尼罗河边缘，开罗以南约450英里处。它们是埃及宗教的中心，建在底比斯的帝国城市中，当时埃及帝国正处于鼎盛时期，是世界上的最强大力量。这是当时的纽约。这些神庙建造了大约2000年。

cues.en: each pharaoh adding his bit, leaving his name in stone to last forever. Inside the temple domain, there were 65 towns, 433 gardens and orchards, 400,000 animals, and it took 80,000 people just to run the place. Small wonder that centuries afterwards, the Greeks and the Romans came here and gawked like peasants at a civilization that made their efforts look like well-dressed mud huts.
cues.zh: 每位法老都添上自己的一笔，把自己的名字刻在石头上，以求永世长存。神庙领地内有65座城镇、433座花园和果园、40万头牲畜，光维持运转就需要8万人。难怪几百年后，希腊人和罗马人来到这里，像乡巴佬一样目瞪口呆地看着一个文明——相比之下，他们的成就不过是穿得整整齐齐的泥棚。

cues.en: It still has that effect today. You come here from the great modern cities, full of the immense power of modern technology at your fingertips, press a button, turn a switch, and this place stops you dead. And then just when you think you've got the measure of Karnak, you come here at dawn to the Hall of Columns, one of the most massive structures ever built. And anything I was going to say isn't enough. Look at it.
cues.zh: 它至今仍有这种效果。你从伟大的现代城市来到这里，指尖满是现代科技的磅礴力量，按个按钮，拨个开关，而这个地方让你戛然而止。就在你以为自己已经摸清了卡纳克神庙的底细时，你在黎明时分来到列柱大厅——有史以来最宏伟的建筑之一。我想说的任何话都不够用。看看它吧。

cues.en: The Egyptians built an empire and ran it with a handful of technology. The wheel, the irrigation canals, the loom, a calendar, pen and ink, some cutting tools, simple metallurgy, and the plough, the invention that triggered it all off. And yet look how complex and sophisticated their civilization was and how soon it happened after that first man-made harvest. The Egyptian plough and those of the few other civilizations that sprang up around the world at the same time.
cues.zh: 埃及人建立了一个帝国，却只靠寥寥几种技术来运转它。轮子、灌溉渠、织布机、历法、笔和墨水、一些切割工具、简单的冶金术，还有犁——引发这一切的发明。然而看看他们的文明多么复杂精妙，而且是在第一次人造丰收之后多么短的时间内就实现了。埃及的犁，以及当时世界各地兴起的少数其他文明的犁。

cues.en: gave us control over nature and at the same time tied us for good to the things that we invent so that tomorrow will be better than today. The Egyptians knew that. That's why they had gods, to make sure their systems didn't fail. Karnak was the first great statement of what technology could do with unlimited manpower and the approval of the gods.
cues.zh: 让我们得以控制自然，同时也把我们永久地绑在了我们所发明的东西上，好让明天比今天更好。埃及人懂得这一点。所以他们才有神，确保他们的系统不会崩溃。卡纳克神庙是第一个伟大的宣言，宣告了技术在无限人力与神明认可之下能成就什么。

cues.en: Ironically, the modern equivalent lies, again, in the desert. This time, the nomads are also settled by a river, a river of oil. But what it took the pharaohs 4,000 years to build took the Kuwaitis 4,000 days. What's happened in Kuwait, the change from a nomadic existence to being able to buy and use everything modern technology has to offer, has come in much less than one generation. Kuwait represents the immense power of technology used in a way most of us have never experienced.
cues.zh: 讽刺的是，现代版的对应物再次出现在沙漠之中。这一次，游牧民族同样傍河而居，一条石油之河。但法老们花了4000年才建成的东西，科威特人只用了4000天。科威特发生的变化——从游牧生活转变为能够购买和使用现代技术所提供的一切——在不到一代人的时间里就完成了。科威特展现了技术的巨大力量，其使用方式是我们大多数人从未经历过的。

cues.en: because we've lived with the kind of change it can bring for more than a hundred years. Here, it's been focused. Change has been instant and total. Kuwait has suddenly become like New York or any other of the great urban islands of technology, totally dependent on that technology. Like them, without it, Kuwait would return to the desert. Hello, Michelle? Hi, how are you?
cues.zh: 因为我们已经在它所能带来的那种变化中生活了一百多年。而在这里，变化是集中的。变化是瞬间的、彻底的。科威特突然变得像纽约或任何其他伟大的城市技术岛屿一样，完全依赖于那种技术。和它们一样，没有它，科威特就会回到沙漠。喂，Michelle？嗨，你好吗？

cues.en: Hey, listen. I'm coming to spend my Christmas in New York, okay? You see how increasingly the only way we in the advanced industrial nations with our bewildering technology network can survive is by selling bewilderment and dependence on technology to the rest of the world? Or is it not bewilderment and dependence, but a healthier, wealthier, better way of living than the old way? And yet, whether or not you dress up technology to look local, the technology network is the same.
cues.zh: 嘿，听着。我要来纽约过圣诞节，好吗？你看到了吗，我们这些发达工业国家拥有令人眼花缭乱的技术网络，而我们生存的唯一方式越来越是向世界其他地方推销这种眼花缭乱和对技术的依赖？或者这不是眼花缭乱和依赖，而是一种比旧方式更健康、更富裕、更好的生活方式？然而，无论你是否把技术打扮成本地化的样子，技术网络都是一样的。

cues.en: And as it spreads, will it spread the ability to use machines as we do without understanding them? Somebody said a few years ago about the way our modern world affects us all. If you understand something today, that means it must already be obsolete. Or to put it another way, never have so many people understood so little about so much.
cues.zh: 随着它传播开去，它会不会也传播这样一种能力：像我们一样使用机器，却并不理解它们？几年前有人谈到现代世界如何影响我们所有人时说：如果你今天懂一件事，那说明它肯定已经过时了。换句话说，从来没有这么多人，对这么多事情，懂得这么少。

cues.en: So why are we in this position? Why is our modern industrialized world the way it is and not some different way with different technology doing different things to us? Well, that's what the rest of this series is going to look at You saw just now that the plow and irrigation kicked us all off and that an invention acts rather like a trigger Because once it's there
cues.zh: 那么，我们为什么会处于这种境地？为什么我们现代工业化世界是这个样子，而不是另一种样子——用不同的技术，对我们产生不同的影响？这正是本系列接下来要探讨的。你刚才看到，犁和灌溉把我们所有人推上了这条路，而一项发明的作用很像一个触发器——因为一旦它出现，

cues.en: It changes the way things are and that change stimulates the production of another invention which in turn causes change and so on. Why those inventions happened between 6000 years ago and now, where they happened and when they happened, is a fascinating blend of accident, genius, craftsmanship, geography, religion, war, money, ambition. Above all, at some point
cues.zh: 它就改变了事物的面貌，而这种改变又刺激了另一项发明的产生，后者又带来改变，如此循环。为什么这些发明发生在六千年前到今天之间，为什么发生在它们发生的地方，为什么发生在它们发生的时间，这是偶然、天才、技艺、地理、宗教、战争、金钱、野心之间一种迷人的交织。最重要的是，在某个时刻——

cues.en: Everybody is involved in the business of change, not just the so-called great men. Given what they knew at the time and a moderate amount of what's up here, I hope to show you that you or I could have done just what they did or come close to it. Because at no time did an invention come out of thin air into somebody's head like that. You just had to put a number of bits and pieces that were already there together in the right way. Following the trail of events...
cues.zh: 每个人都卷入到变革这件事里，而不只是所谓的伟人。考虑到他们当时所知道的，再加上这里的一点东西，我希望向你们表明：你或我本可以做出他们所做的，或者接近做到。因为从来没有哪项发明是那样凭空出现在某人脑子里的。你只需要把已经存在的许多零碎东西，以正确的方式拼在一起。沿着事件的脉络……

cues.en: from some point in the past to a piece of modern technology is rather like a detective story with you as the detective knowing only as much as the people in the past knew and like them having to guess at what was likely to happen next so the trigger that sets off the first of those detective stories is that and I'd like to leave you with one question before next time why does a modern invention
cues.zh: 从过去的某个时刻到一项现代技术，这更像是一个侦探故事，而你就是侦探，只知道过去人们所知道的事情，像他们一样必须猜测接下来可能发生什么，所以引发第一个侦探故事的触发点就是这个，我想在下次之前留给你们一个问题：为什么一项现代发明

cues.en: that fundamentally affects the lives of every single human being on this planet begin 2,600 years ago with somebody doing this.
cues.zh: 从根本上影响着这个星球上每一个人的生活，却始于2600年前某个人做这个动作。
